levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. The Fysbis malware is known to be a modular Linux trojan/backdoor that implements plug-in and controller modules as distinct classes. It includes both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of ELF binaries and can install itself with or without root privileges.

Your goal is to identify and investigate the suspicious activity, determine the extent of the compromise, and take appropriate containment measures. You will encounter service names, timer names, and port numbers as flags during this investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.
levels.solution:
To identify the suspicious service, you can use the following command:

`systemctl list-units --type=service --all`

Look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations. The flag is the name of the suspicious service: `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by understanding the concept of systemd services and how they are managed.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be related to the suspicious activity you observed.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: You have identified a suspicious service running on the target host. Determine how this service is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution:
To determine the persistence mechanism, you can use the following command:

`systemctl list-timers`

Look for any timers that are associated with the suspicious service. The flag is the persistence mechanism: `systemd timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Consider how services can be configured to start automatically after a system reboot.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Systemd timers are often used to schedule tasks and maintain service persistence.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Investigate the network traffic associated with the suspicious service to determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication.
levels.solution:
To investigate the network traffic, you can use the following command:

`ss -tulnp`

Look for any connections that are associated with the suspicious service. The flag is the network port used for the suspicious communication: `80`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Understand the concept of network sockets and how they are used for communication.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Network monitoring tools can help you capture and analyze traffic from the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all network connections.
